title: When the String Pool is not beneficial
answer: The String Pool is useful when many equal String values are reused, especially literals, because those equal values can share one canonical object. Explicit interning is less useful when strings are highly dynamic, mostly unique, short-lived, or created in very large numbers, because there is little duplicate storage to eliminate while interning still requires String-table lookup and management. It is also inappropriate for sensitive data such as passwords. Use `intern()` only when measurements show substantial repetition and a real memory benefit; do not intern every dynamic String by default.
